items.title: Skin in a London winter
items.intro: Central heating, cold wind and the Tube: what we change on the menu from November.

sections.heading: What changes
sections.text:
Most clients tell us their skin feels tight by December. We move more people to the hydrating facial, and use a richer mask.

We also do fewer peels in the darkest weeks, simply because people forget the SPF.

sections.heading: At home
sections.text: Keep what you use simple. If something new stings, stop and tell us.

pages.title: Skin by season
pages.description: What Clémence changes on the menu through the year, season by season.
pages.intro: London skin changes with the weather and the heating. So does our menu.

blocks.heading: Winter
blocks.body:
December to February. Central heating, cold wind and the Tube: most clients tell us their skin feels tight. We move more people to the hydrating facial and use a richer mask and a longer massage.

We do fewer light peels in the darkest weeks, because SPF is the first thing people forget in winter. If you want a peel, we book it with the patch test and send the evening advice on WhatsApp.

blocks.heading: Spring
blocks.body:
March to May. The best time for a course of four light peels, a month apart, finished before the long days. We start each course with the patch test 48 hours before the first.

Brows and lashes get busy from April, for holidays and weddings. Book the lash lift and tint at least a week before you travel.

blocks.heading: Summer
blocks.body:
June to August. Lighter facials, more calming ones, and SPF at the end of every treatment. No peels within two weeks of a holiday in the sun.

The back facial and body scrub are most asked for now. Waxing: book two days before the beach, not the day before.

blocks.heading: Autumn
blocks.body:
September to November. After the summer, many clients come back to the deep-cleanse facial, then to their usual rhythm: every four to six weeks, as each card on our menu says.

This is when we plan winter: the hydrating course, and gift days booked before Christmas.
